notes: Modified cash basis village audit. Governmental lines from the governmental funds Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances (p5 major funds, p6 Non-Major and Total Governmental Funds column; the total column is mislabelled '2032' for 2023). Taxes 223,723 split by Schedule 1 totals (p11: Property tax 110,067 + Motor vehicle tax 12,601 + Sales tax 101,055; nonmajor funds have no taxes); Intergovernmental revenues 108,248 split by p11 (Highway allocation 82,203 + Motor vehicle fees 5,535 + Homestead allocation 10,323 + Other 10,187). Principal (25,000) and interest (12,424) paid by the Street fund are printed under Other financing sources (uses) and recorded in other_financing. Beginning/ending cash from the governmental funds cash statement Total assets 2022/2023 columns (p4; cash in bank + county treasurer, no investments); fund balances recorded separately (p6). Business-type from Exhibit H (modified cash, ties to the Statement of Activities p2: charges 251,987, expenses 303,967, transfers 82,591, net position 154,034 -> 184,645); principal paid 70,000 and capital purchases 110,424 are on the cash flow statement only. Balance sheet from the government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1) because it includes capital assets and debt (funds statement totals 634,539 differ). Detail: Schedule 1 per major fund (p10), Combining non-major schedule per fund (p12-13; Keno fund had no activity, balance 3,805), Exhibit H per proprietary fund (p8). Schedule 5 (p14, budget by fund group, totals only) and Schedule 6 (p15, proprietary totals budget-basis) not recorded to avoid double counting. Read pages 1-15 of 15
